From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, Nov 01 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: FRAUD ALERT: SpectraAI signup cluster flagged for promo credits

Hi Grace / Marissa,

Automated anomaly detector flagged a cluster of trial signups tied to SpectraAI requesting self-serve promo credits. Summary: 27 accounts created in a 2 hour window, 18 from the same /24 CIDR, multiple disposable/alias domains (spectraai-*.mailinator[.]com variants), and identical device fingerprints for 14 accounts. Token consumption patterns show high-volume refreshes immediately after credit issuance.

I attached a CSV with the accounts and a short screenshot of activity. Recommendation: hold manual issuance and run an investigator review before granting any additional credits.

Attachments: spectraai_suspect_signups_20261101.csv (csv), account_activity_snip_20261101.png (png)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Xy_example_report
Jira: INFRA-7241

Cheers,
Dev
Senior Trust & Safety Engineer

Subject: RE: FRAUD ALERT: SpectraAI signup cluster flagged for promo credits

Team —
I dug in and appended risk buckets in the CSV (bot-like, disposable-domain, shared-device). Findings:
- 19/27 accounts show disposable/throwaway email patterns and MX records pointing to temporary-messaging providers.
- The 8 accounts with company domain emails (spectraai.com) were created after the cluster and have low activity; they do not match the device fingerprints from the bulk accounts.
- IP reversal: the majority resolve to cloud VPS providers commonly used in automated signup farms; two IPs map to a North America hosting provider with recent abuse reports.
- Token usage: peak bursts immediately after promo credit issuance in earlier clusters (pattern matches known abuse signatures).

Given the signal strength, I recommend denying a manual override. If Sales wants to proceed, require: (1) org-level verification (e.g., Domain WHOIS + contracts email), (2) SSO or verified business email whitelist, and (3) start with a paid pilot or tightly-scoped sandbox rather than open self-serve credits.

Attached: spectraai_suspect_signups_20261101.csv, account_activity_snip_20261101.png
Jira: INFRA-7241 (triage underway)

—Dev

Date: Tue, Nov 02 2026 15:40:17 -0000
Subject: RE: FRAUD ALERT: SpectraAI signup cluster flagged for promo credits

Thanks everyone for the quick triage. I reviewed Dev's findings and agree with the deny recommendation. The disposable-domain and shared-device signals are strong enough that a one-time manual promo override presents an unacceptable fraud risk.

Marissa — please offer SpectraAI an expedited verification path:
- Organize a 30-minute verification call with Elaine to confirm company details and procurement timeline;
- Ask SpectraAI to provide a contracts email + proof of incorporation or a signed MSA if they want trial expansion;
- Offer a 14-day paid pilot (discounted) instead of an open promo grant; we'll fast-track enablement and provide a sandbox environment.

If Sales returns verified company artifacts and the accounts reconcile to company-owned emails and IPs, we can reopen the exception review. For now, deny the self-serve credit issuance.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
